title: Sysprose verify report
description: What `npm run sysprose -- verify <file> --json` emits on stdout. The top-level `verdict` block is the exit-code arithmetic and is the ONLY thing an automation needs to read: `verdict.exitCode` is what the process exited with, including the degraded-model rule that lowers a clean sweep to 2. Read docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md's `verify` section for the contract in words — its 1 means REFUTED, which is not what the reporting subcommands' 1 means.

ok.description: Did the file load cleanly? False ⇒ `verdict.exitCode` is 2.

degraded.description: Present only when the model did not load cleanly. A verdict over half a model is not a verdict, so its presence forces exit 2.

discharged.description: Obligations discharged non-vacuously BY THE ENGINE THAT WAS ASKED FOR. Under `--engine literal` a `holds-at-values` row counts; under `smt` and `auto` it does not.

violated.description: Refuted with every feature at its model value. Nothing else is exit 1.

inconclusive.description: Everything undecided, vacuous and tool-absent included. Any un-forgiven one is exit 2.

designAdmitted.description: Refutations obtained under `--free`: a design the model admits, exit 2, never 1.

engine.description: What `auto` resolved to. It resolves to `smt` or reports `verification/tool-absent`; it NEVER falls back to `literal`.

forgiven.description: How many inconclusive rows `--allow-inconclusive` lowered. It lowers `verification/timeout` and `verification/unsupported-construct` and nothing else.

exitCode.description: The obligations and the verification cases together, under the ordering the contract states — 1 beats 2 beats 0, which is not the numeric order. The top-level `verdict.exitCode` is this one with the degraded-model rule applied, and it is the one the process exits with. A model that declares no verification case is decided by its obligations alone, because `cases.exitCode` is 0 over an empty list.

timeoutMs.description: The per-check budget the SMT engine ran under, or `null` when no solver ran — the literal engine evaluates at the model's own values and has nothing to bound, and so does an `auto` run that found no backend. Every check in the solver lane IS bounded and there is no spelling for "no timeout", so a row reported `verification/timeout` was decided by nothing but this number.

strictVacuity.description: Was `--strict-vacuity` given? It promotes a vacuity row to `verification/vacuous-property`, an error, and changes NOTHING else — not the claim, not `discharged`, not the exit code.

caseReport.description: The verification cases the model declares, each with a computed verdict. ALWAYS PRESENT, and empty for a model that declares none.

notPerformed.description: Cases the method gate refused to judge because this tool performs analysis only. Always inconclusive, always exit 2, and `--allow-inconclusive` never lowers one: an unjudged case is not a refutation, and it is not a forgivable undecidedness either.

exitCode.description: What the cases contribute to the run: 1 for a case the model refutes, 2 for one this tool would not or could not judge, 0 when every case passed AND when there is no case at all.

caseId.description: Present only under `--case REF`: the element id the report was narrowed to. Element ids are fresh on every load (D3), so key on `case` instead — this is here to join the report to the rest of one run, never to identify a case across runs.

case.description: Present only under `--case REF`: the QUALIFIED NAME the report was narrowed to, the same value a record's `flags.case` carries. This is the field a consumer can key on.

method.description: What the case's `@VerificationCases::VerificationMethod { kind = …; }` says, READ rather than judged. `analyze` is the only method this tool performs.

unrecognised.description: Spellings that name no `VerificationMethodKind` this tool knows. They are reported, never read as `analyze`: an unrecognised kind fails towards not-performed.

judged.description: False only for a method gate — a different fact from an inconclusive verdict. One says the tool did not look; the other says it looked and could not tell.

verdict.description: The library `PassIf` reading, over the engine that was asked for. This is the word the exit code is computed from.

facet.description: The word that may be WRITTEN INTO THE FILE, which is the stricter question: `pass` only when every obligation was `proved`. Under `--engine literal` a case is legitimately `verdict: pass` and `facet: inconclusive`.

facets.description: The PER-REQUIREMENT roll-up the verdict facet is written from: one entry per verified requirement, with the facet ITS own rows reach. `facet: null` means this run produced no obligation row for that requirement, and nothing is written onto it — a case's word is a summary over a set, and stamping it onto a member the run never looked at would put a `pass` on a requirement nobody checked.

changed.description: `verdict` facets already in the file that say something other than what this run computed. Reported, never rewritten here.

premises.description: The assumptions, evaluated BEFORE the guarantee. A pass that stands on three assumptions is a different claim from an unconditional one.

witness.description: The solver's own model, in the magnitudes the file stores: the counterexample for a refutation, the satisfiable-assumptions witness for a proof. Empty for every literal-engine row and for any SMT row no check answered `sat` on.

tautology.description: `check(¬G)` alone was unsat: the goal is true of every model, so it is honestly proved and says nothing about THIS design. Always false from the literal engine, which never proves anything.

core.description: The `:named` labels of the unsat core the solver returned for THIS proof, sorted, each `kind:qualifiedName` over the kinds `axiom`, `premise`, `goal` and `side`. Non-empty only on a `proved` row; `verify --why` is what prints it. It is a SUFFICIENT reason the solver chose and NOT the set of assumptions the claim depends on — an axiom listed may not have been needed, and an axiom not listed may still carry the claim — and its membership is the solver's own choice rather than a property of the model, which is why no evidence record carries one. A `side:` member is an assumption the ENCODING added (a non-zero divisor) and shares its qualified name with the axiom it guards, so a consumer keying on the name alone loses it. It is present on EVERY `--json` payload, with `--why` and without it — the flag gates the text display and not the field — so a consumer that renders these members carries the sufficiency sentence itself: on the text path the tool prints it under every core, and here it exists only in this description.

axiomCensus.description: How far this obligation's answer narrowed the model's axiom set, or `null` where no script was built for the row — four zeroes would be a measurement, and there was none. `coreAxioms` is read against `footprintAxioms`, and equal means the solver narrowed nothing beyond the read-closure the encoder already applies; a `coreAxioms` BELOW `footprintAxioms` is not by itself solver narrowing, because a kept row the encoder refused asserts nothing and can never be named.

modelAxioms.description: Every axiom row this run gathered from the model, whether the encoder took it or refused it — the denominator `--why` prints.

footprintAxioms.description: The axiom rows this obligation's read-closure kept. It INCLUDES rows the encoder refused, which are carried so a refutation can be judged against the whole context and which put no assertion in the script.

scriptAxioms.description: The assertions those kept rows actually put in the script, side conditions included. So it exceeds `footprintAxioms` wherever a kept axiom divides by a variable (measured: 5 against a footprint of 4 on `examples/uav-isr.sysml`'s endurance obligation) and falls below it wherever a kept axiom was refused (measured: 1 against 2 on `test/fixtures/verification/models/refused-axiom-relevant.sysml`).

coreAxioms.description: How many `axiom:` labels the solver's own unsat core named. 0 wherever none did — including every row that is not `proved`.
